newsitem.title: UK: Downing Street denies Euro-role for BP head.
newsitem.headline: Downing Street denies Euro-role for BP head.

text.p: Officials in new British Prime Minister Tony Blair's office said press reports that British Petroleum Co Plc chairman Sir David Simon had been asked to become minister for European affairs were incorrect.
"He is not going to be a minister," a senior Downing Street source said.

He told reporters there had been discussions about whether Simon, a strong supporter of a single European currency, should have some sort of role, but the report in Saturday's Financial Times newspaper was wrong.
Downing Street sources said Simon was not expected to join Blair's policy unit either.
A BP spokesman said earlier that Simon had been in talks with Blair's office and would like to be involved in shaping Britain's relationship with the European Union.
But he was also keen to continue his involvement with BP.
If Simon had been appointed, it would have indicated that Labour was more sympathetic about a single currency than its public rhetoric had suggested.

He has been one of the most prominent advocates of British participation in monetary union, arguing that it would reduce costs for business and give Britain a better chance of sustaining a sound monetary policy and low inflation.
